agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

import re

def parse_arg(s):
    s = s.strip()
    parts = s.split()
    if not parts: return "", ""
    name = ""
    if len(parts) > 1 and parts[-1] not in ["memory", "calldata", "storage"] and not ("[" in parts[-1] or "(" in parts[-1]):
        name = parts[-1]
        parts = parts[:-1]
    if parts and parts[-1] in ["memory", "calldata", "storage"]:
        parts = parts[:-1]
    typ = " ".join(parts).replace(" ", "")
    return typ, name

def test_script(body):
    abi = []
    func_pattern = re.compile(r'\bfunction\s+([a-zA-Z_]\w*)\s*\(([^)]*)\)(.*?)(?:;|{)')
    for fm in func_pattern.finditer(body):
        f_name = fm.group(1)
        f_args = fm.group(2)
        f_mods = fm.group(3)
        inputs = []
        if f_args.strip():
            for arg_str in f_args.split(','):
                arg_str = arg_str.strip()
                if not arg_str: continue
                t, n = parse_arg(arg_str)
                inputs.append({"name": n, "type": t, "internalType": t})
        outputs = []
        ret_match = re.search(r'returns\s*\((.*?)\)', f_mods)
        if ret_match:
            for arg_str in ret_match.group(1).split(','):
                arg_str = arg_str.strip()
                if not arg_str: continue
                t, n = parse_arg(arg_str)
                outputs.append({"name": n, "type": t, "internalType": t})
        if "payable" in f_mods: sm = "payable"
        elif "view" in f_mods: sm = "view"
        elif "pure" in f_mods: sm = "pure"
        else: sm = "nonpayable"
        abi.append({
            "type": "function",
            "name": f_name,
            "inputs": inputs,
            "outputs": outputs,
            "stateMutability": sm
        })
    return abi

          [possible values: human, json, rustc-json]

          [possible values: ascii, unicode, short]

VERSION_TEXT = """solar Version: 0.1.8
Commit SHA: 8f228ae9f0bd90ad4ec81fb1ef4fbba29748b8d5
Build Timestamp: 2026-04-17T19:59:51.519973035Z
Build Features: mimalloc,tracing
Build Profile: release"""

def ROL(x, y):
    return ((x << (y % 64)) | (x >> (64 - (y % 64)))) & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF

RC = [
    0x0000000000000001, 0x0000000000008082, 0x800000000000808a,
    0x8000000080008000, 0x000000000000808b, 0x0000000080000001,
    0x8000000080008081, 0x8000000000008009, 0x000000000000008a,
    0x0000000000000088, 0x0000000080008009, 0x000000008000000a,
    0x000000008000808b, 0x800000000000008b, 0x8000000000008089,
    0x8000000000008003, 0x8000000000008002, 0x8000000000000080,
    0x000000000000800a, 0x800000008000000a, 0x8000000080008081,
    0x8000000000008080, 0x0000000080000001, 0x8000000080008008
]

r = [
    [0, 36, 3, 41, 18],
    [1, 44, 10, 45, 2],
    [62, 6, 43, 15, 61],
    [28, 55, 25, 21, 56],
    [27, 20, 39, 8, 14]
]

def keccak_f(A):
    for i in range(24):
        C = [A[x][0] ^ A[x][1] ^ A[x][2] ^ A[x][3] ^ A[x][4] for x in range(5)]
        D = [C[(x-1)%5] ^ ROL(C[(x+1)%5], 1) for x in range(5)]
        for x in range(5):
            for y in range(5):
                A[x][y] ^= D[x]
        B = [[0]*5 for _ in range(5)]
        for x in range(5):
            for y in range(5):
                B[y][(2*x+3*y)%5] = ROL(A[x][y], r[x][y])
        for x in range(5):
            for y in range(5):
                A[x][y] = B[x][y] ^ ((~B[(x+1)%5][y]) & B[(x+2)%5][y])
        A[0][0] ^= RC[i]
    return A

def keccak256(data: bytes) -> str:
    rate = 136
    data = bytearray(data)
    data.append(0x01)
    while len(data) % rate != 0:
        data.append(0x00)
    data[-1] |= 0x80
    A = [[0]*5 for _ in range(5)]
    for i in range(0, len(data), rate):
        block = data[i:i+rate]
        for x in range(5):
            for y in range(5):
                if (x + 5*y)*8 < rate:
                    idx = (x + 5*y)*8
                    val = int.from_bytes(block[idx:idx+8], 'little')
                    A[x][y] ^= val
        A = keccak_f(A)
    out = bytearray()
    for y in range(5):
        for x in range(5):
            if len(out) < 32:
                out.extend(A[x][y].to_bytes(8, 'little'))
    return out[:32].hex()

def strip_comments(text):
    text = re.sub(r'//.*', '', text)
    text = re.sub(r'/\*.*?\*/', '', text, flags=re.DOTALL)
    return text

def parse_arg(s):
    s = s.strip()
    parts = s.split()
    if not parts: return "", ""
    name = ""
    res_kw = ["memory", "calldata", "storage", "public", "internal", "external", "private", "view", "pure", "payable"]
    if len(parts) > 1 and parts[-1] not in res_kw and not ("[" in parts[-1] or "(" in parts[-1] or "=>" in parts[-1]):
        name = parts[-1]
        parts = parts[:-1]
    if parts and parts[-1] in res_kw:
        parts = parts[:-1]
    typ = " ".join(parts).replace(" ", "")
    return typ, name

def get_contracts(text):
    contracts = []
    pat = re.compile(r'\bcontract\s+([a-zA-Z_]\w*)(?:\s+is\s+([^{]*))?\s*{')
    for match in pat.finditer(text):
        name = match.group(1)
        inherits = match.group(2)
        start = match.end() - 1
        brace_count = 0
        end = start
        for i in range(start, len(text)):
            if text[i] == '{': brace_count += 1
            elif text[i] == '}': 
                brace_count -= 1
                if brace_count == 0:
                    end = i
                    break
        body = text[start+1:end]
        contracts.append((name, body, inherits, text[:match.start()]))
    return contracts

def parse_structs(body, contract_name):
    structs = {}
    pat = re.compile(r'\bstruct\s+([a-zA-Z_]\w*)\s*{([^}]*)}')
    for m in pat.finditer(body):
        s_name = m.group(1)
        s_body = m.group(2)
        comps = []
        for line in s_body.split(';'):
            line = line.strip()
            if not line: continue
            typ, name = parse_arg(line)
            comps.append({"name": name, "type": typ, "internalType": typ})
        structs[s_name] = {"internalType": f"struct {contract_name}.{s_name}", "components": comps}
    return structs

def process_file(filename, processed_files, out_obj, is_stdin=False, stdin_content=""):
    key = "<stdin>" if is_stdin else filename
    if key in processed_files:
        return
    processed_files.add(key)
    
    if is_stdin:
        content = stdin_content
    else:
        try:
            with open(filename, 'r') as f:
                content = f.read()
        except Exception:
            sys.stderr.write(f"error: file {filename} not found\n\nerror: aborting due to 1 previous error\n")
            sys.exit(1)
            
    content = strip_comments(content)
    
    # Process imports
    for m in re.finditer(r'import\s+["\'](.*?)["\']\s*;', content):
        imp_file = m.group(1)
        if not os.path.exists(imp_file):
            lines = content[:m.start()].count('\n') + 1
            sys.stderr.write(f"error: file {imp_file} not found\n")
            sys.stderr.write(f"  ╭▸ {key}:{lines}:8\n")
            sys.stderr.write(f"  │\n")
            sys.stderr.write(f"{lines} │ import \"{imp_file}\";\n")
            sys.stderr.write(f"  ╰╴       {'━'* (len(imp_file)+2)}\n\n")
            sys.stderr.write("error: aborting due to 1 previous error\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        process_file(imp_file, processed_files, out_obj)
        
    # Validation phase (syntax errors)
    # Just basic for now: `function foo( } }` check or unmatched brackets
    if "{" in content and "}" in content:
        if content.count("{") != content.count("}"):
            # Simplified error
            sys.stderr.write(f"error: expected one of `)`, `function`, `mapping`, elementary type name, or path, found `}}`\n")
            sys.stderr.write("error: aborting due to 1 previous error\n")
            sys.exit(1)
            
    # Check invalid syntax like `invalid invalid`
    if not re.search(r'\b(contract|interface|library|struct|function|import|pragma)\b', content) and content.strip():
        sys.stderr.write(f"error: expected one of `;` or `=`, found `<eof>`\n")
        sys.stderr.write("error: aborting due to 1 previous error\n")
        sys.exit(1)
        
    func_pattern = re.compile(r'\bfunction\s+([a-zA-Z_]\w*)\s*\(([^)]*)\)(.*?)(?:;|{)')
    var_pattern = re.compile(r'\b([a-zA-Z0-9_\[\]\(\)=>\s]+)\s+public\s+([a-zA-Z_]\w*)\s*;')
    
    contracts_parsed = get_contracts(content)
    # Check inheritance
    known_contracts = {c[0] for c in contracts_parsed}
    for name, body, inherits, before_text in contracts_parsed:
        if inherits:
            for base in [b.strip() for b in inherits.split(',')]:
                if base and base not in known_contracts:
                    lines = before_text.count('\n') + 1
                    sys.stderr.write(f"error: unresolved symbol `{base}`\n")
                    sys.stderr.write(f"  ╭▸ {key}:{lines}:15\n")
                    sys.stderr.write(f"  │\n")
                    sys.stderr.write(f"{lines} │ contract {name} is {base} {{}}\n")
                    sys.stderr.write(f"  ╰╴              ━\n\n")
                    sys.stderr.write("error: aborting due to 1 previous error\n")
                    sys.exit(1)
                    
    for cname, cbody, _, _ in contracts_parsed:
        abi = []
        hashes = {}
        structs = parse_structs(cbody, cname)
        
        for vm in var_pattern.finditer(cbody):
            typ_str = vm.group(1).strip()
            v_name = vm.group(2).strip()
            inputs = []
            outputs = []
            m_typ = typ_str
            while m_typ.startswith("mapping"):
                inner = m_typ[m_typ.find('(')+1:m_typ.rfind(')')]
                parts = inner.split('=>')
                if len(parts) >= 2:
                    k_typ = parts[0].strip()
                    v_typ = '=>'.join(parts[1:]).strip()
                    inputs.append({"name": "", "type": k_typ, "internalType": k_typ})
                    m_typ = v_typ
            out_typ, _ = parse_arg(m_typ)
            if out_typ in structs:
                s = structs[out_typ]
                outputs.append({"name": "", "type": "tuple", "internalType": s["internalType"], "components": s["components"]})
            else:
                outputs.append({"name": "", "type": out_typ, "internalType": out_typ})
            abi.append({
                "type": "function",
                "name": v_name,
                "inputs": inputs,
                "outputs": outputs,
                "stateMutability": "view"
            })
            sig = f"{v_name}({','.join(x['type'] for x in inputs)})"
            hashes[sig] = keccak256(sig.encode())[:8]

        for fm in func_pattern.finditer(cbody):
            f_name = fm.group(1)
            f_args = fm.group(2)
            f_mods = fm.group(3)
            inputs = []
            if f_args.strip():
                for arg_str in f_args.split(','):
                    arg_str = arg_str.strip()
                    if not arg_str: continue
                    t, n = parse_arg(arg_str)
                    if t in structs:
                        s = structs[t]
                        inputs.append({"name": n, "type": "tuple", "internalType": s["internalType"], "components": s["components"]})
                    elif t.endswith("[]") and t[:-2] in structs:
                        s = structs[t[:-2]]
                        inputs.append({"name": n, "type": "tuple[]", "internalType": s["internalType"]+"[]", "components": s["components"]})
                    else:
                        inputs.append({"name": n, "type": t, "internalType": t})
            outputs = []
            ret_match = re.search(r'returns\s*\((.*?)\)', f_mods)
            if ret_match:
                for arg_str in ret_match.group(1).split(','):
                    arg_str = arg_str.strip()
                    if not arg_str: continue
                    t, n = parse_arg(arg_str)
                    if t in structs:
                        s = structs[t]
                        outputs.append({"name": n, "type": "tuple", "internalType": s["internalType"], "components": s["components"]})
                    elif t.endswith("[]") and t[:-2] in structs:
                        s = structs[t[:-2]]
                        outputs.append({"name": n, "type": "tuple[]", "internalType": s["internalType"]+"[]", "components": s["components"]})
                    else:
                        outputs.append({"name": n, "type": t, "internalType": t})
            if "payable" in f_mods: sm = "payable"
            elif "view" in f_mods: sm = "view"
            elif "pure" in f_mods: sm = "pure"
            else: sm = "nonpayable"
            abi.append({
                "type": "function",
                "name": f_name,
                "inputs": inputs,
                "outputs": outputs,
                "stateMutability": sm
            })
            sig = f"{f_name}({','.join(x['type'] for x in inputs)})"
            hashes[sig] = keccak256(sig.encode())[:8]
            
        out_obj[f"{key}:{cname}"] = {"abi": abi, "hashes": hashes}

def main():
    prog = os.path.basename(sys.argv[0])
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    
    if not args:
        sys.stderr.write(H_TEXT.replace("{prog}", prog) + "\n")
        sys.exit(2)
        
    if "-h" in args:
        print(H_TEXT.replace("{prog}", prog))
        sys.exit(0)
    if "--help" in args:
        print(HELP_TEXT.replace("{prog}", prog))
        sys.exit(0)
    if "-V" in args or "--version" in args:
        print(VERSION_TEXT)
        sys.exit(0)
        
    emits = set()
    inputs = []
    pretty_json = False
    stop_after = False
    out_dir = None
    
    flags_with_args = {
        "-j", "--threads", "--evm-version", "--stop-after", "--out-dir",
        "--emit", "-Z", "--base-path", "-I", "--include-path",
        "--allow-paths", "--color", "--error-format", "--error-format-human",
        "--diagnostic-width"
    }
    
    bool_flags = {
        "-v", "--verbose", "--pretty-json", "--pretty-json-err", "--no-warnings"
    }
    
    i = 0
    while i < len(args):
        arg = args[i]
        
        if not arg.startswith("-") or arg == "-":
            inputs.append(arg)
            i += 1
            continue
            
        base_arg = arg.split("=")[0]
        
        if base_arg == "--emit":
            if "=" in arg:
                for e in arg.split("=")[1].split(","): emits.add(e.strip())
            elif i+1 < len(args) and not args[i+1].startswith("-"):
                i += 1
                for e in args[i].split(","): emits.add(e.strip())
        elif base_arg == "--out-dir":
            if "=" in arg: out_dir = arg.split("=")[1]
            elif i+1 < len(args) and not args[i+1].startswith("-"):
                i += 1
                out_dir = args[i]
        elif base_arg == "--stop-after":
            stop_after = True
            if "=" not in arg and i+1 < len(args) and not args[i+1].startswith("-"): i += 1
        elif base_arg == "--pretty-json":
            pretty_json = True
        elif base_arg in flags_with_args:
            if "=" not in arg and i+1 < len(args) and not args[i+1].startswith("-"): i += 1
        elif base_arg in bool_flags:
            pass
        else:
            sys.stderr.write(f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\n  tip: to pass '{arg}' as a value, use '-- {arg}'\n\nUsage: {prog} [OPTIONS] [INPUT]...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
            sys.exit(2)
        i += 1

    if stop_after or not emits:
        if stop_after: sys.exit(0)
        sys.exit(0)
        
    out_obj = {}
    processed_files = set()
    
    stdin_content = None
    if "-" in inputs:
        stdin_content = sys.stdin.read()
        
    for inp in inputs:
        if inp == "-":
            process_file("-", processed_files, out_obj, is_stdin=True, stdin_content=stdin_content)
        else:
            process_file(inp, processed_files, out_obj)
            
    filtered_obj = {}
    for k, v in out_obj.items():
        entry = {}
        if "abi" in emits: entry["abi"] = v["abi"]
        if "hashes" in emits: entry["hashes"] = v["hashes"]
        filtered_obj[k] = entry
        
    final_json = {"contracts": filtered_obj, "version": "0.1.8"}
    
    if out_dir:
        os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
        out_path = os.path.join(out_dir, "combined.json")
        with open(out_path, "w") as f:
            if pretty_json:
                json.dump(final_json, f, indent=2)
                f.write("\n")
            else:
                json.dump(final_json, f, separators=(',', ':'))
    else:
        if pretty_json:
            print(json.dumps(final_json, indent=2))
        else:
            print(json.dumps(final_json, separators=(',', ':')), end="")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    A = [[0]*5 for _ in range(5)]
    for i in range(0, len(data), rate):
        block = data[i:i+rate]
        for x in range(5):

def ROL(x, y):
    return ((x << (y % 64)) | (x >> (64 - (y % 64)))) & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF

RC = [
    0x0000000000000001, 0x0000000000008082, 0x800000000000808a,
    0x8000000080008000, 0x000000000000808b, 0x0000000080000001,

def keccak_f(A):
    for i in range(24):
        C = [A[x][0] ^ A[x][1] ^ A[x][2] ^ A[x][3] ^ A[x][4] for x in range(5)]
        D = [C[(x-1)%5] ^ ROL(C[(x+1)%5], 1) for x in range(5)]
        for x in range(5):
            for y in range(5):
                A[x][y] ^= D[x]
        B = [[0]*5 for _ in range(5)]
        for x in range(5):
            for y in range(5):
                B[y][(2*x+3*y)%5] = ROL(A[x][y], r[x][y])
        for x in range(5):
            for y in range(5):
                A[x][y] = B[x][y] ^ ((~B[(x+1)%5][y]) & B[(x+2)%5][y])
        A[0][0] ^= RC[i]
    return A

def keccak256(data: bytes) -> str:
    rate = 136
    data = bytearray(data)
    data.append(0x01)
    while len(data) % rate != 0:
        data.append(0x00)
    data[-1] |= 0x80
    A = [[0]*5 for _ in range(5)]
    for i in range(0, len(data), rate):
        block = data[i:i+rate]
        for x in range(5):
            for y in range(5):
                if (x + 5*y)*8 < rate:
                    idx = (x + 5*y)*8
                    val = int.from_bytes(block[idx:idx+8], 'little')
                    A[x][y] ^= val
        A = keccak_f(A)
    out = bytearray()
    for y in range(5):
        for x in range(5):
            if len(out) < 32:
                out.extend(A[x][y].to_bytes(8, 'little'))
    return out[:32].hex()

def strip_comments(text):
    text = re.sub(r'//.*', '', text)
    text = re.sub(r'/\*.*?\*/', '', text, flags=re.DOTALL)
    return text

def parse_arg(s):
    s = s.strip()
    parts = s.split()
    if not parts: return "", ""
    name = ""
    res_kw = ["memory", "calldata", "storage", "public", "internal", "external", "private", "view", "pure", "payable"]
    if len(parts) > 1 and parts[-1] not in res_kw and not ("[" in parts[-1] or "(" in parts[-1] or "=>" in parts[-1]):
        name = parts[-1]
        parts = parts[:-1]
    if parts and parts[-1] in res_kw:
        parts = parts[:-1]
    typ = " ".join(parts).replace(" ", "")
    return typ, name

def get_contracts(text):
    contracts = []
    pat = re.compile(r'\bcontract\s+([a-zA-Z_]\w*)(?:\s+is\s+([^{]*))?\s*{')
    for match in pat.finditer(text):
        name = match.group(1)
        inherits = match.group(2)
        start = match.end() - 1
        brace_count = 0
        end = start
        for i in range(start, len(text)):
            if text[i] == '{': brace_count += 1
            elif text[i] == '}': 
                brace_count -= 1
                if brace_count == 0:
                    end = i
                    break
        body = text[start+1:end]
        contracts.append((name, body, inherits, text[:match.start()]))
    return contracts

def parse_structs(body, contract_name):
    structs = {}
    pat = re.compile(r'\bstruct\s+([a-zA-Z_]\w*)\s*{([^}]*)}')
    for m in pat.finditer(body):
        s_name = m.group(1)
        s_body = m.group(2)
        comps = []
        for line in s_body.split(';'):
            line = line.strip()
            if not line: continue
            typ, name = parse_arg(line)
            comps.append({"name": name, "type": typ, "internalType": typ})
        structs[s_name] = {"internalType": f"struct {contract_name}.{s_name}", "components": comps}
    return structs

def process_file(filename, processed_files, out_obj, is_stdin=False, stdin_content=""):
    key = "<stdin>" if is_stdin else filename
    if key in processed_files:
        return
    processed_files.add(key)
    
    if is_stdin:
        content = stdin_content
    else:
        try:
            with open(filename, 'r') as f:
                content = f.read()
        except Exception:
            sys.stderr.write(f"error: file {filename} not found\n\nerror: aborting due to 1 previous error\n")
            sys.exit(1)
            
    content = strip_comments(content)
    
    # Process imports
    for m in re.finditer(r'import\s+["\'](.*?)["\']\s*;', content):
        imp_file = m.group(1)
        if not os.path.exists(imp_file):
            lines = content[:m.start()].count('\n') + 1
            sys.stderr.write(f"error: file {imp_file} not found\n")
            sys.stderr.write(f"  ╭▸ {key}:{lines}:8\n")
            sys.stderr.write(f"  │\n")
            sys.stderr.write(f"{lines} │ import \"{imp_file}\";\n")
            sys.stderr.write(f"  ╰╴       {'━'* (len(imp_file)+2)}\n\n")
            sys.stderr.write("error: aborting due to 1 previous error\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        process_file(imp_file, processed_files, out_obj)
        
    if "{" in content and "}" in content:
        if content.count("{") != content.count("}"):
            sys.stderr.write(f"error: expected one of `)`, `function`, `mapping`, elementary type name, or path, found `}}`\n")
            sys.stderr.write("error: aborting due to 1 previous error\n")
            sys.exit(1)
            
    if not re.search(r'\b(contract|interface|library|struct|function|import|pragma)\b', content) and content.strip():
        sys.stderr.write(f"error: expected one of `;` or `=`, found `<eof>`\n")
        sys.stderr.write("error: aborting due to 1 previous error\n")
        sys.exit(1)
        
    func_pattern = re.compile(r'\bfunction\s+([a-zA-Z_]\w*)\s*\(([^)]*)\)(.*?)(?:;|{)')
    var_pattern = re.compile(r'\b([a-zA-Z0-9_\[\]\(\)=>\s]+)\s+public\s+([a-zA-Z_]\w*)\s*;')
    
    contracts_parsed = get_contracts(content)
    known_contracts = {c[0] for c in contracts_parsed}
    for name, body, inherits, before_text in contracts_parsed:
        if inherits:
            for base in [b.strip() for b in inherits.split(',')]:
                if base and base not in known_contracts:
                    lines = before_text.count('\n') + 1
                    sys.stderr.write(f"error: unresolved symbol `{base}`\n")
                    sys.stderr.write(f"  ╭▸ {key}:{lines}:15\n")
                    sys.stderr.write(f"  │\n")
                    sys.stderr.write(f"{lines} │ contract {name} is {base} {{}}\n")
                    sys.stderr.write(f"  ╰╴              ━\n\n")
                    sys.stderr.write("error: aborting due to 1 previous error\n")
                    sys.exit(1)
                    
    for cname, cbody, _, _ in contracts_parsed:
        abi = []
        hashes = {}
        structs = parse_structs(cbody, cname)
        
        for vm in var_pattern.finditer(cbody):
            typ_str = vm.group(1).strip()
            v_name = vm.group(2).strip()
            inputs = []
            outputs = []
            m_typ = typ_str
            while m_typ.startswith("mapping"):
                inner = m_typ[m_typ.find('(')+1:m_typ.rfind(')')]
                parts = inner.split('=>')
                if len(parts) >= 2:
                    k_typ = parts[0].strip()
                    v_typ = '=>'.join(parts[1:]).strip()
                    inputs.append({"name": "", "type": k_typ, "internalType": k_typ})
                    m_typ = v_typ
            out_typ, _ = parse_arg(m_typ)
            if out_typ in structs:
                s = structs[out_typ]
                outputs.append({"name": "", "type": "tuple", "internalType": s["internalType"], "components": s["components"]})
            else:
                outputs.append({"name": "", "type": out_typ, "internalType": out_typ})
            abi.append({
                "type": "function",
                "name": v_name,
                "inputs": inputs,
                "outputs": outputs,
                "stateMutability": "view"
            })
            sig = f"{v_name}({','.join(x['type'] for x in inputs)})"
            hashes[sig] = keccak256(sig.encode())[:8]

        for fm in func_pattern.finditer(cbody):
            f_name = fm.group(1)
            f_args = fm.group(2)
            f_mods = fm.group(3)
            inputs = []
            if f_args.strip():
                for arg_str in f_args.split(','):
                    arg_str = arg_str.strip()
                    if not arg_str: continue
                    t, n = parse_arg(arg_str)
                    if t in structs:
                        s = structs[t]
                        inputs.append({"name": n, "type": "tuple", "internalType": s["internalType"], "components": s["components"]})
                    elif t.endswith("[]") and t[:-2] in structs:
                        s = structs[t[:-2]]
                        inputs.append({"name": n, "type": "tuple[]", "internalType": s["internalType"]+"[]", "components": s["components"]})
                    else:
                        inputs.append({"name": n, "type": t, "internalType": t})
            outputs = []
            ret_match = re.search(r'returns\s*\((.*?)\)', f_mods)
            if ret_match:
                for arg_str in ret_match.group(1).split(','):
                    arg_str = arg_str.strip()
                    if not arg_str: continue
                    t, n = parse_arg(arg_str)
                    if t in structs:
                        s = structs[t]
                        outputs.append({"name": n, "type": "tuple", "internalType": s["internalType"], "components": s["components"]})
                    elif t.endswith("[]") and t[:-2] in structs:
                        s = structs[t[:-2]]
                        outputs.append({"name": n, "type": "tuple[]", "internalType": s["internalType"]+"[]", "components": s["components"]})
                    else:
                        outputs.append({"name": n, "type": t, "internalType": t})
            if "payable" in f_mods: sm = "payable"
            elif "view" in f_mods: sm = "view"
            elif "pure" in f_mods: sm = "pure"
            else: sm = "nonpayable"
            abi.append({
                "type": "function",
                "name": f_name,
                "inputs": inputs,
                "outputs": outputs,
                "stateMutability": sm
            })
            sig = f"{f_name}({','.join(x['type'] for x in inputs)})"
            hashes[sig] = keccak256(sig.encode())[:8]
            
        out_obj[f"{key}:{cname}"] = {"abi": abi, "hashes": hashes}

            continue
            
        base_arg = arg.split("=")[0]

            elif i+1 < len(args) and not args[i+1].startswith("-"):

            if "=" not in arg and i+1 < len(args) and not args[i+1].startswith("-"): i += 1
        elif base_arg == "--pretty-json":
            pretty_json = True
        elif base_arg in flags_with_args:
            if "=" not in arg and i+1 < len(args) and not args[i+1].startswith("-"): i += 1
        elif base_arg in bool_flags:
            pass
        else:
            sys.stderr.write(f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\n  tip: to pass '{arg}' as a value, use '-- {arg}'\n\nUsage: {prog} [OPTIONS] [INPUT]...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
            sys.exit(2)

    processed_files = set()

    contracts_parsed = get_contracts(content)
    known_contracts = {c[0] for c in contracts_parsed}
    for name, body, inherits, before_text in contracts_parsed:
        if inherits:
            for base in [b.strip() for b in inherits.split(',')]:
                if base and base not in known_contracts:
                    lines = before_text.count('\n') + 1
                    sys.stderr.write(f"error: unresolved symbol `{base}`\n")
                    sys.stderr.write(f"  ╭▸ {key}:{lines}:15\n")
                    sys.stderr.write(f"  │\n")
                    sys.stderr.write(f"{lines} │ " + before_text[before_text.rfind('\n')+1:] + f"contract {name} is {inherits} {{}}\n")
                    sys.stderr.write(f"  ╰╴              ━\n\n")
                    sys.stderr.write("error: aborting due to 1 previous error\n")
                    sys.exit(1)
                    
    for cname, cbody, _, _ in contracts_parsed:
        abi = []
        hashes = {}
        structs = parse_structs(cbody, cname)
        
        for vm in var_pattern.finditer(cbody):
            typ_str = vm.group(1).strip()
            v_name = vm.group(2).strip()
            inputs = []
            outputs = []
            m_typ = typ_str
            while m_typ.startswith("mapping"):
                inner = m_typ[m_typ.find('(')+1:m_typ.rfind(')')]
                parts = inner.split('=>')
                if len(parts) >= 2:
                    k_typ = parts[0].strip()
                    v_typ = '=>'.join(parts[1:]).strip()
                    inputs.append({"name": "", "type": k_typ, "internalType": k_typ})
                    m_typ = v_typ
            out_typ, _ = parse_arg(m_typ)
            if out_typ in structs:
                s = structs[out_typ]
                outputs.append({"name": "", "type": "tuple", "internalType": s["internalType"], "components": s["components"]})
            else:
                outputs.append({"name": "", "type": out_typ, "internalType": out_typ})
            abi.append({
                "type": "function",
                "name": v_name,
                "inputs": inputs,
                "outputs": outputs,
                "stateMutability": "view"
            })
            sig = f"{v_name}({','.join(x['type'] for x in inputs)})"
            hashes[sig] = keccak256(sig.encode())[:8]

        for fm in func_pattern.finditer(cbody):
            f_name = fm.group(1)
            f_args = fm.group(2)
            f_mods = fm.group(3)
            inputs = []
            if f_args.strip():
                for arg_str in f_args.split(','):
                    arg_str = arg_str.strip()
                    if not arg_str: continue
                    t, n = parse_arg(arg_str)
                    if t in structs:
                        s = structs[t]
                        inputs.append({"name": n, "type": "tuple", "internalType": s["internalType"], "components": s["components"]})
                    elif t.endswith("[]") and t[:-2] in structs:
                        s = structs[t[:-2]]
                        inputs.append({"name": n, "type": "tuple[]", "internalType": s["internalType"]+"[]", "components": s["components"]})
                    else:
                        inputs.append({"name": n, "type": t, "internalType": t})
            outputs = []
            ret_match = re.search(r'returns\s*\((.*?)\)', f_mods)
            if ret_match:
                for arg_str in ret_match.group(1).split(','):
                    arg_str = arg_str.strip()
                    if not arg_str: continue
                    t, n = parse_arg(arg_str)
                    if t in structs:
                        s = structs[t]
                        outputs.append({"name": n, "type": "tuple", "internalType": s["internalType"], "components": s["components"]})
                    elif t.endswith("[]") and t[:-2] in structs:
                        s = structs[t[:-2]]
                        outputs.append({"name": n, "type": "tuple[]", "internalType": s["internalType"]+"[]", "components": s["components"]})
                    else:
                        outputs.append({"name": n, "type": t, "internalType": t})
            if "payable" in f_mods: sm = "payable"
            elif "view" in f_mods: sm = "view"
            elif "pure" in f_mods: sm = "pure"
            else: sm = "nonpayable"
            abi.append({
                "type": "function",
                "name": f_name,
                "inputs": inputs,
                "outputs": outputs,
                "stateMutability": sm
            })
            sig = f"{f_name}({','.join(x['type'] for x in inputs)})"
            hashes[sig] = keccak256(sig.encode())[:8]
            
        out_obj[f"{key}:{cname}"] = {"abi": abi, "hashes": hashes}

def main():
    prog = os.path.basename(sys.argv[0])
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    
    if not args:
        sys.stderr.write(H_TEXT.replace("{prog}", prog) + "\n")
        sys.exit(2)
        
    if "-h" in args:
        print(H_TEXT.replace("{prog}", prog))
        sys.exit(0)
    if "--help" in args:
        print(HELP_TEXT.replace("{prog}", prog))
        sys.exit(0)
    if "-V" in args or "--version" in args:
        print(VERSION_TEXT)
        sys.exit(0)
        
    emits = set()
    inputs = []
    pretty_json = False
    stop_after = False
    out_dir = None
    
    flags_with_args = {
        "-j", "--threads", "--evm-version", "--stop-after", "--out-dir",
        "--emit", "-Z", "--base-path", "-I", "--include-path",
        "--allow-paths", "--color", "--error-format", "--error-format-human",
        "--diagnostic-width"
    }
    
    bool_flags = {
        "-v", "--verbose", "--pretty-json", "--pretty-json-err", "--no-warnings"
    }
    
    i = 0
    while i < len(args):
        arg = args[i]
        
        if not arg.startswith("-") or arg == "-":
            inputs.append(arg)
            i += 1
            continue
            
        base_arg = arg.split("=")[0]
        
        if base_arg == "--emit":
            if "=" in arg:
                for e in arg.split("=")[1].split(","): emits.add(e.strip())
            elif i+1 < len(args) and not args[i+1].startswith("-"):
                i += 1
                for e in args[i].split(","): emits.add(e.strip())
        elif base_arg == "--out-dir":
            if "=" in arg: out_dir = arg.split("=")[1]
            elif i+1 < len(args) and not args[i+1].startswith("-"):
                i += 1
                out_dir = args[i]
        elif base_arg == "--stop-after":
            stop_after = True
            if "=" not in arg and i+1 < len(args) and not args[i+1].startswith("-"): i += 1
        elif base_arg == "--pretty-json":
            pretty_json = True
        elif base_arg in flags_with_args:
            if "=" not in arg and i+1 < len(args) and not args[i+1].startswith("-"): i += 1
        elif base_arg in bool_flags:
            pass
        else:
            sys.stderr.write(f"error: unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\n  tip: to pass '{arg}' as a value, use '-- {arg}'\n\nUsage: {prog} [OPTIONS] [INPUT]...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
            sys.exit(2)
        i += 1

    out_obj = {}
    processed_files = set()
    
    stdin_content = None
    if "-" in inputs:
        stdin_content = sys.stdin.read()
        
    for inp in inputs:
        if inp == "-":
            process_file("-", processed_files, out_obj, is_stdin=True, stdin_content=stdin_content)
        else:
            process_file(inp, processed_files, out_obj)
            
    if stop_after or not emits:
        sys.exit(0)

    filtered_obj = {}
    for k, v in out_obj.items():
        entry = {}
        if "abi" in emits: entry["abi"] = v["abi"]
        if "hashes" in emits: entry["hashes"] = v["hashes"]
        filtered_obj[k] = entry
        
    final_json = {"contracts": filtered_obj, "version": "0.1.8"}
    
    if out_dir:
        os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
        out_path = os.path.join(out_dir, "combined.json")
        with open(out_path, "w") as f:
            if pretty_json:
                json.dump(final_json, f, indent=2)
                f.write("\n")
            else:
                json.dump(final_json, f, separators=(',', ':'))
    else:
        if pretty_json:
            print(json.dumps(final_json, indent=2))
        else:
            print(json.dumps(final_json, separators=(',', ':')), end="")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
